_about: The love hub (plan 7.6f). The rows are defined by the Hebrew and Greek: a verb row by who loves (agent) or what is loved (patient) in out/frames.jsonl.gz, a noun row by the words standing in the noun's own phrase (MACULA's clauses), an adjective row by the same. The first row a verse matches takes it; a verse no row takes is listed under 'More'. A word counts only where its verse renders it in this sense ('sense'): אהב as 'friend' and φιλέω as 'kiss' are not this concept. 'doors' are the cards a row opens. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/love.json. Design: ontology/provenance/concept-hubs/concept-hubs.html (Doug, 2026-10-09: 'love it').
_shown_why: Doug, 2026-10-09: 'approve of the contents of both'

titles.noun: What the text says of love

others._why: Doug, 2026-10-09: 'focus on agape love and then have a section at the bottom for other uses of the English word love'. The rows stand on אהב and the agape words (the Greek Old Testament renders the one by the other in the greatest commandment); φιλέω, חֶסֶד, דּוֹד and the rest are different words, named apart with their verses. h4993 is a gloss stray ('you.love?' on a name).
